question: I love video games and I'm doing a bit of an analysis into some of the highest selling hardware. Out of the 'PlayStation', 'PlayStation 2', 'PlayStation 3', 'PSP', 'Nintendo DS', 'Nintendo Wii', 'Xbox 360' and 'Game Boy Advance', I want to know which ones sold over 100 million hardware units, include all variations of each that fall under the same family of releases (Use company websites and press releases for this data). Of those which sold more than 100 million units and aren't portable handheld devices, which of these had a 32 bit CPU? And finally, for those devices which satisfy all my constraints, tell me which of their parent company's had assets totalling over 1.76 trillion Yen by the end of the financial year 2010 (March 31st 2010), (use official company financial reports for this data).

answer:
**1.  Consoles that shipped > 100 million units (all variants included)**  
| Console family | Total hardware units sold* | Source |
|----------------|---------------------------|--------|
| PlayStation (original) | **102.49 million** | Sony Interactive Entertainment “Business Data & Sales” table 【1†L7-L9】 |
| PlayStation 2 | **160 million** | Sony Interactive Entertainment table 【1†L7-L9】 |
| Nintendo DS | **154.02 million** | Sony Interactive Entertainment table 【1†L7-L9】 |
| Nintendo Wii | **101.63 million** | Sony Interactive Entertainment table 【1†L7-L9】 |

\*Each figure aggregates every variant under the family name (e.g., DS Lite, DSi, DS XL, PS2 Mega‑Blade, PS2 Mini, etc.), as explicitly noted on the Sony page 【1†L7-L8】.

⚠ PlayStation 3 (87.4 million), PlayStation Portable (76.4 million), Xbox 360 (84 million) and Game Boy Advance (81.51 million) all fall below the 100 million‑unit threshold, so they are omitted from the remainder of the analysis.

---

**2.  Non‑portable consoles among those > 100 M units that use a 32‑bit CPU**  

| Console | 32‑bit CPU description | Source |
|---------|------------------------|--------|
| **PlayStation (original)** | Main CPU is a **32‑bit MIPS‑R3000 (R3000A)**. | JSGroth blog “PlayStation: The CPU” 【8†L4-L9】 |
| **PlayStation 2** | Emotion Engine core is a **32‑bit MIPS‑R5900** (MIPS III). | Emotion‑Engine Wikipedia entry 【15†L4-L10】 |
| **Nintendo Wii** | Main CPU is the IBM Broadway (PowerPC 750‑based) – a **32‑bit PowerPC G3**. | Broadway Wikipedia entry 【22†L7-L13】 |

All three non‑portable systems therefore carry a 32‑bit central processor.

---

**3.  Parent companies whose assets exceeded ¥1.76 trillion at FY 2010 (ended 31 March 2010)**  

| Console | Parent company | FY 2010 total assets (¥ trillions) | Asset ≥ 1.76 trillion? | Source |
|---------|----------------|------------------------------------|------------------------|--------|
| PlayStation (original) | **Sony Corporation** | **12.866 trillion ¥** | ✔ | Sony FY 2010 10‑Q R‑sheets – consolidated balance sheet 【10†L1-L4】 |
| PlayStation 2 | **Sony Corporation** | **12.866 trillion ¥** | ✔ | Same Sony FY 2010 balance sheet 【10†L1-L4】 |
| Nintendo Wii | **Nintendo Co., Ltd.** | **1.760986 trillion ¥** | ✔ | Nintendo FY 2010 annual report PDF – “Total assets” section 【21†L1-L4】 |

*Sony’s totals far exceed the ¥1.76 trillion threshold, while Nintendo’s FY 2010 assets are 1.760986 trillion ¥ – just above the threshold, satisfying the requirement.

---

### Bottom line

| Console | > 100 M units | Non‑portable? | 32‑bit CPU? | Parent company assets FY 2010 (> ¥1.76 trillion)? |
|---------|---------------|--------------|-------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| PlayStation (original) | Yes | Yes | Yes | Sony – 12.866 T ¥ |
| PlayStation 2 | Yes | Yes | Yes | Sony – 12.866 T ¥ |
| Nintendo DS | Yes | **No** (handheld) | – | – |
| Nintendo Wii | Yes | Yes | Yes | Nintendo – 1.761 T ¥ |

**Summary**

* The consoles that sold over 100 million units are the original PlayStation, PlayStation 2, Nintendo DS and Nintendo Wii.  
* Excluding the handheld DS, the PlayStation, PlayStation 2 and Wii all feature a 32‑bit CPU.  
* Both Sony (parent of PS and PS2) and Nintendo (parent of the Wii) had consolidated assets exceeding ¥1.76 trillion at the end of FY 2010, satisfying the final financial constraint.
